bug_semantics: Cargo CanonicalUrl always chopped a trailing .git from registry index URLs. That is correct for git indexes, where host/index and host/index.git are the same repository, but wrong for sparse indexes, which are ordinary HTTPS paths and treat those URLs as distinct registries. SourceId equality and hashing use kind plus CanonicalUrl, so sparse+https://host/index and sparse+https://host/index.git intern as the same identity and share the configured Cargo token. An attacker who can publish on a sparse registry that allows cross-registry dependencies and who can host a sibling *.git sparse index requiring auth can publish a crate depending on the sibling; when the victim fetches it, Cargo sends the victim's token to the malicious index.
flaw_origin: Unconditional .git chopping began as git-only ident canonicalization (e2191677381b4a0c7de6a354ef3741d71306d990 in git/source.rs, extracted into CanonicalUrl by e54541225142b509f5f3b7468897b2c31a7635dc). The HTTP/sparse registry feature 412b6339147265743488cb2fe6073cc250fdf7f0 (rust-lang/cargo#10470) first built SourceIds from sparse+http(s) URLs and ran them through CanonicalUrl::new without gating .git chopping on protocol; it also stripped the sparse+ prefix after chopping. Parent 109bfbd055325ef87a6e7f63d67da7e838f8300b has no sparse SourceId parsing, no http_remote.rs, and no sparse+ handling. Later 16ad1f2945dff5c7f3234257d5ab477ea86b7338 kept the sparse+ prefix on CanonicalUrl but left .git chopping unconditional, so the credential collision between sparse URLs survived until the 2026 fix.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-5222/GHSA-p688-r7jv-fm6f is a real published CWE-647 in Cargo sparse-index URL canonicalization, not a withdrawn/rejected advisory. Cargo treated sparse+https://host/index and sparse+https://host/index.git as one SourceId because CanonicalUrl stripped .git from every URL, including those with a protocol specifier, and SourceId identity is kind+CanonicalUrl. The attacker path is a sibling sparse index whose download endpoint records the reused token. The 2026 fix (c4d63a442, merged 03cb632e on master as #17031; 1.96/0.97.0 backport 3c51f26a2 via 30a34c682) keeps .git chopping only when the scheme has no '+'. BIC choice: the smallest public commit that first applied that git-only canonicalizer to sparse registry URLs is 412b6339147265743488cb2fe6073cc250fdf7f0, the HTTP registry implementation. Its parent lacks sparse SourceIds and http_remote.rs, so the collision cannot exist before this commit. Earlier needs_chopping writes are git-only and are not this CVE; later SparseRegistry / keep-sparse+ refactors did not introduce the .git collision. 412b63391 is the sole #10470 member in cargo.git. AI judgment is from that commit object only: human author/committer Arlo Siemsen with no AI/co-author/bot markers, so NOT_AI.
